How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.content:
Below is everything you’ll need to hit the **“get information of an interface”** endpoint on your Cisco Nexus‑Dashboard appliance running v6.3.1 at `192.120.45.67`. --- ### 1️⃣ Build the full URI | Component | Value | |-----------|-------| | Base host | `https://192.120.45.67` | | Path | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` | | Query parameters |   - `fabricName=Network1`
  - `nodeId=12`
  - `podId=10`
  - `interfaceType=Ethernet`
  - `infoType=Speed` | > **Resulting URL:** > ``` > https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed > ``` --- ### 2️⃣ Authentication & Headers Cisco Nexus‑Dashboard uses OAuth2 Bearer tokens (or sometimes basic auth depending on configuration). Typical headers: ```http Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN # <-- replace with real token Accept: application/json # optional – defaults to JSON Content-Type: application/json # not required for GET ``` If you’re testing locally and don’t care about SSL validation, add `--insecure` (`-k`) to curl or set `verify=False` in Python’s `requests`. --- ### 3️⃣ Sample Requests #### A. Using *cURL* (command line) ```bash curl --request GET \ --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \ --header "Accept: application/json" \ --insecure \ # skip cert check (optional) "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` Replace `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN` with the actual JWT/OAuth token issued by the dashboard. #### B. Using *Python* (`requests` lib) ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo" PARAMS = { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "Ethernet", # case-sensitive as per spec "infoType": "Speed" } HEADERS = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", # TOKEN = your access token "Accept": "application/json" } response = requests.get(BASE_URL, params=PARAMS, headers=HEADERS, verify=False) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` Again, swap out `TOKEN` for whatever credential method your environment requires. --- ### 4️⃣ What You Should See A successful call will return HTTP status **200 OK** along with a JSON payload similar to: ```json { "fabricName":"Network1", "nodeId":12, "podId":10, "interfaces":[ { "name":"Eth1000/1", "speedMbps":40000 } ] } ``` (Exact structure depends on the current data model.) --- ### 5️⃣ Common Pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |------|-----| | “401 Unauthorized” | Verify token validity / scopes | | “404 Not Found” | Double‑check the exact path – it can differ between firmware releases | | “SSL error” | Use `--insecure` or supply CA bundle (`certifi.where()`) | | Wrong parameter names | Parameters are case‑sensitive; refer to the official docs for spelling | --- That’s all! Once you’ve got this working, you can script it, embed it into dashboards, or automate monitoring tasks across your Fabric. Happy querying!
